product: Buy 1  Hammer Miner DC06 and get a Free Bitaxe V2

messages.text: Hi Ali — I'm Sarah, an AI researcher with HeliumDeploy. Thank you so much for taking 25 minutes to do this — it really means a lot.
Right on. Okay. So let's discuss it.

Awesome. So I was looking through your browsing history before this call — you spent a LOT of time on the site back in March, looking at a bunch of different products. I want to dig into that.

Let me pull up one that caught my eye — you came back to it a bunch of times. Have you seen this one — the NerdQaxe + Gamma + Hammer bundle?
Yes. I have seen that one. And the price seems a little high for me right now.
Got it — too high right now. What's "right now" about it? Like, is there a specific budget number in your head, or is it more about timing?
I'm only looking to spend around three hundred dollars as I'm just getting started in this

Ah okay — so you're just getting started. That changes things.

What pulled you toward this bundle specifically then? Because $650 is double your budget — but you kept coming
I was interested in seeing what it was all about, and I did some research. And I understand that for um, Dogecoin, that's a very low power hash rate.

Wait — Dogecoin? The Hammer Miner in this bundle does Dogecoin/Litecoin (Scrypt), but the NerdQaxe and Bitaxe are Bitcoin (SHA-256). Were you specifically looking for a Dogecoin miner, or Bitcoin, or both?
I was looking for both.
Got it — both. So when you say $300 budget for getting started, are you imagining splitting that across two miners (one BTC + one DOGE), or picking one to start?
I definitely wanna gear towards BTC to start. Um, After I get going for a while, then I'll eventually transition into different cryptocurrencies. But I'm not sold on Dodge and Litecoin just yet.
Makes sense — BTC first, branch out later. Let me show you the one most folks getting started land on. This is the Bitaxe Gamma — $95, well under your $300. Have you looked at this one specifically?
I actually own one of these already. I also own the nerd quacks. Plus plus rev six and the oct ax y. And I wanna get another OctaX.

Wait — hold on. You already own a Gamma, a NerdQaxe++ Rev 6, AND a NerdOctaxe? And you want ANOTHER Octaxe?

That's a serious stack already. I thought you said you were just getting started — what does "getting started" mean to you then?

I know in the big picture, my seventeen terahash a second is a drop in the ocean, and I wanna add more hash to my current hash rate. I know that uh, OktaX will only add about ten to eleven terahash a second but I'm working on building up My goal is to hit two hundred and fifty to three hundred terahash a second.

Okay — 250 to 300 TH/s is a real goal. That reframes everything.

So at 17 TH/s now, adding another Octaxe gets you to ~27. To hit 250-300, you'd need way more than just Octaxes — that's like 25+ more of them. What's the actual plan to get there? Are you stacking Octaxes one by one, or are you eyeing something bigger like an Avalon Q or an S19?

Exactly. I'm eyeing something bigger, but I wanna make sure that it's very efficient, period. I don't have I don't have a lot of money to spend, so that's why I'm starting with these smaller purchases. Eventually, I want to purchase an Avalon q

Got it — Avalon Q is the endgame. Let me pull it up. $1,700 for 90 TH/s. So one of these gets you from 17 to 107 — basically a third of your goal in one purchase. Why are you stacking small Octaxes for $469 a pop instead of saving up for this? The math is way better — $19/TH on the Avalon vs ~$47/TH on the Octaxe.

Well, I don't make a lot of money, so I'm working on saving up As of right now, my goal is to get one more Octax and then I wanna point them all towards Bitcoin Cash Solo pool in hopes of making or actually in hopes of solving a block so I can make the funds to buy the Avalon queue.

Ohhh — okay. So the Octaxes aren't just stacking hashrate, they're a lottery play on Bitcoin Cash to FUND the Avalon Q. That's a whole different strategy.

Why Bitcoin Cash specifically? Why not point them at BTC solo?

Well, currently, my three minors are pointed to BTC solo, but I know the chances are much slimmer for BTC over Bitcoin Cash. That's why I wanna go for Bitcoin Cash first because the chances are much better for me to hit a block and I feel I'd be able to hit a block within a month or two.

Smart — leveraging the lower difficulty on BCH. That's a real solo-lottery strategy, not just hopium.

Where'd you learn that move? Like, who taught you to think about pool difficulty math like that — Discord, YouTube, Reddit?
All of the above, plus I've been using ChatGPT and Grok to help me analyze the different avenues and perspectives of mining for crypto.
Interesting — so you're using ChatGPT and Grok as part of your research process. What do you ask them that you can't get from Discord or YouTube?
They help me minimize the amount of time I would spend on YouTube or Discord by scouring the Internet for me and pulling all of the information into a easy to digest format.

That's a really useful frame — they're a time-compression tool, not a replacement for the community.

So when you're using ChatGPT or Grok to research a miner — like before you bought the Octaxe — what does that actually look like? Are you asking it "what's the best miner under $X" or are you cross-checking specs you already saw, or something else?

Both of those that you just mentioned, I'm also checking for vendors who are reputable And I'm also checking for probability and power consumption Lastly, I'm checking for devices and how much heat they produce because I live in Florida, and heat producing devices are not good down here. Um, it's already very hot, and I already pay a lot in my air conditioning bill.

Florida — okay, that's huge. Heat is a real constraint for you, not just a nice-to-have.

So with summer coming up in Florida — are you planning to keep all your miners running, or are you thinking about scaling down till fall?
I plan on keeping them all running I have a little fan pointed at them to keep them cool. And I am not running them hard. So their temperature is staying rather cool.

So you're underclocking them to ride out the Florida summer. Smart.

How far down are you running them? Like, are you at stock and just adding a fan, or are you actually in the firmware turning voltage/frequency down?

I used chat GPT and Groc to figure out what's the best frequency to run these devices, and I tune them to a specific frequency and voltage. The bigger ones are tuned at about five hundred and fifty to six hundred frequency. And about twelve hundred voltage The B. Gamma is set to factory default.

Okay so you're hands-on in AxeOS — tuning frequency and voltage on the NerdQaxes. That's deep tinkering territory.

What's the next mod you're planning on them? Custom cooling, heatsinks, something else?

I need to learn more about heat sinks, so that'll be later on down the road. For now, I did buy a nice shelf to put the devices on that allows good airflow and ventilation. And I plan on adding another small fan or two to the shelf to help with that airflow and ventilation.
Nice — purpose-built shelf with airflow. Where does the shelf live in the house? Like what room?
It's in the living room. It's close to an AC vent and a ceiling fan. I also have a small fan currently underneath the octacks.

Living room — interesting. So these aren't tucked away in a closet or garage, they're out in the main space.

Is that on purpose? Like, do you want them visible — conversation piece, you like looking at them — or is it just the best spot for cooling?
It's actually the best spot for my Wi Fi because it's closest to my Wi Fi router without getting in the way of my living space or my pets. It's also nice to be able to see them.

Both — proximity to WiFi AND you like seeing them. Got it.

On the WiFi point — are all three miners running on WiFi right now? Any drops or connectivity issues?
Yes. They are all running on Wi Fi, and no connectivity issues or drops that I'm aware of.

Okay good. Let me show you something we're considering — curious if it'd be useful to you. It's a small Ethernet adapter, about $35, that snaps onto a miner so you can run wired instead of WiFi. Given your setup is right next to the router and WiFi's been fine — would you actually buy one of these?
No. I don't think I would ever buy one of those.

Fair enough — solid no. Good signal for us.

Let me switch gears. You mentioned reputable vendors as one of your research criteria. Besides HeliumDeploy, who else are you checking when you're shopping for miners?

I'm strictly checking to make sure they are reputable and have a positive history. When I was searching, I found a s l miner dot com. And I purchased one device from them. I also found another company in Ireland. I forget their name. I also purchased a product from them. My first product I purchased was from Bitcoin miner or it's called actually bitcoinmerch dot com. But they are way overpriced. I was looking at Helium Deploy, and I noticed you guys have good sales every now and then. And I'm in the market right now to possibly purchase another Octax.

Got it — so you've already bought from SoloMiners, an Irish vendor, and Bitcoin Merch. And you're price-sensitive enough that HD's sales are what's pulling you in.

The I. one — is it Power Mining? Or someone else?
Someone else.

Okay — if you remember the name later, drop it in. We try to track who else folks are buying from.

When you compare HD to those other vendors — SoloMiners, Bitcoin Merch, the Irish one — what does HD actually do better in your eyes? You said Bitcoin Merch is overpriced, so price is part of it — but what else?

They seem to have a really good community and when I was watching one of their streams on disc Discord, they seemed to have a good following And the community having their back says a lot about the reputation of the company. So that's one reason I keep coming back to Helium Deploy.
"The community having their back" — that's a really specific signal. Say more about that. What did you actually see on the Discord stream that made you think that?

There seemed to be regulars on the disk Discord stream, and the two owners who were streaming uh, the event, uh, seemed to recognize their regular customers. And that to me showed a level of trust that I wanted to see.

That's gold — the founders recognizing regulars by name on a livestream. That's a really specific trust signal.

Was that a Friday night Helium Deploy stream, or someone else's stream they were guesting on?

It was one of their streams where they were giving away a miner, but I can't recall what night of the week it was. I believe it was for they gave away two minors, I believe, And one was like a heater, and the other one was, I believe, a Dodge coin. Hammer.

Yeah — the giveaways. Okay.

So you watched the whole stream waiting for the giveaway? Or you stumbled into it? How'd you even find out it was happening?

I somehow got an alert from this Discord that they were I think I saw it on Discord or maybe it was somewhere else, but I I got an alert, I believe, that said to join the stream And, uh, I I joined it, and that's when I saw it was a giveaway. And, um, yeah. That was it.

Got it. So question for you — when you were doing all that research with ChatGPT and Grok, comparing miners, checking power consumption and probabilities — did you ever land on HD's homepage and use the comparison table there? Or did you do all the comparing externally?
I don't recall that I used h HD's comparison tool I believe I did it all on my own, uh, mostly using chat GPT.

Let me show you what's there — curious if it would've been useful. This is the side-by-side on the homepage. Take a look — what's missing for you? Like, if you were doing this comparison in ChatGPT, what columns would you have asked it about that aren't here?
Heat production is one I that's missing. Uh, outside of that, this pretty much has all the information

Heat production — yeah, makes total sense given Florida. That's a great gap to flag.

What unit would you want it in? Like BTU/hr, or just a temperature range, or watts-as-proxy-for-heat?

That I wouldn't be able to answer. I don't think I know enough about heat production and and that whole thing to be able to comment on that. I think the company, Helium Deploy, and the founders would have a better idea and knowledge of what to call it.

Fair — you want to see it, you trust HD to figure out the right unit. Got it.

Let me show you one more thing — curious about your reaction. We're thinking about adding a leaderboard like this inside the customer dashboard — opt-in, ranks everyone's hashrate, you can see where YOU stand. Given your 250-300 TH/s goal, would you actually use this?

Not me, per personally because I don't care about what other people are doing in that regard. I just wanna know that I'm doing good and wanna see that my machines are running with low errors and good hash rate and good efficiency.

Clean no. You're focused inward — your own machines, your own numbers, not the leaderboard. Good signal.

So on that — what ARE you using to monitor your own machines? Just the AxeOS web interface, or something on top of that?
I only use the web interface to change the pool settings, Primarily, I use HashWatcher, and I pay two ninety nine or two dollars and ninety nine cents a month, so I can monitor more than two devices.
Nice — so you're paying for HashWatcher Pro. What pushed you to upgrade from the free tier — was it specifically hitting the 2-device limit, or was there a feature you wanted?

It was hitting the two device limit. I wanted to be able to monitor all three devices in one place. And see everything And I like having the app because it makes it easy to digest versus the web page where you have to jump between three different tabs. I wish that Helium Deploy offered some sort of app like that that would allow me not only to view my miners while I'm at home, but also to view them while I'm away from home. Would be awesome.

That's a really concrete wish — an HD-branded monitoring app that works at home AND remote. Let me dig into that.

When you're away from home and you check HashWatcher — what are you actually checking for? Like what's the worry that makes you open the app?

I wanna make sure my devices are still connected and running smoothly. I wanna make sure that the temperature is staying current and just to be sure that they're running. It would also be nice to know in case I did hit a block that I would be able to get a notification while I'm away from home.

Block-found notification — okay, that's a big one. Especially since you're running BCH solo lottery with the Octaxes.

Does HashWatcher do that for you right now, or is that a gap?
That's a gap.
Got it — a real gap. So right now if you hit a block on BCH while you're at work, you'd find out... how? Just by checking the pool dashboard later?
Or by checking my crypto wallet.

Oof — so the discovery moment for the thing you've been chasing for months would just be... seeing a balance change. That's anticlimactic for what's supposed to be a lottery win.

Let me ask — when you imagine actually hitting that block, what's the first thing you'd do with the funds? You mentioned buying the Avalon Q — is that immediate, or are there other things in the queue first?

That's pretty immediate. I really want to scale up and go for the big Bitcoin block So I wanna try to work to get my hash rate up to two to three hundred terahash a second. That's my ultimate goal. I know I'm far from it, and I know I have a long way to go. But eventually, I plan on getting there because I wanna eventually buy a property where I can have my own solar to offset some of the cost

Now we're getting somewhere. So the real endgame isn't 300 TH/s — it's an off-grid solar mining property.

Where are you in that journey? Like, is the property a 5-year plan, 10-year, "someday"? And are you already researching solar setups, or is that the phase AFTER you hit hashrate?
That'll probably be the phase after I hit hash rate, and that's a ten plus year goal. Nothing in the immediate

Got it — 10+ year horizon, solar comes after hashrate. Real long-game thinking.

Okay let me zoom back to right now. You said you're in the market for another Octaxe. What's stopping you from pulling the trigger today? Is it purely waiting for the next HD sale, or something else?

Waiting for the HD sale, but also making sure I have enough extra money to splurge on something that's not a necessity. Because I do have two pets and life being so expensive lately. I wanna make sure I have enough to cover all of my expenses to include food for my pets.

Totally fair — pets and bills first, miner second. That's the honest order of things.

When HD does the next sale, how will you actually know it's happening? Email, Discord, the livestream, something else?

I don't like receiving emails because I receive way too many as it is. And notifications as well. I get way too many. So I do check the website periodically, and I think that the discord would probably be the best way to go because that just shows a little badge doesn't give me an alert

Smart — Discord badge over email noise. That tracks with someone who's overwhelmed by inbox volume.

Are you actively in the HD Discord right now, or do you just hop in for streams?
I only hop in for streams.

Got it. So you're aware of the Discord but not really living in it day-to-day.

This has been incredibly helpful, Ali — you've given me a ton to work with. Before we wrap up, is there anything we didn't cover that you wish we had? Anything on your mind about HD, your setup, mining in general?

No. I think we've pretty much covered it all. I think that I um, if Helium Deploy maybe broaden their uh, let me think about it, broaden their items list to offer more products, I think that would be great. I think currently, they are fairly limited on what items they offer. It would be nice to have a little bit more variety Though I'm not sure it would be to their advantage as a customer. It just would be nice to see more variety and have more options.
Got it — broader catalog, more variety. Any specific category you're feeling the gap in? Like is it more miners, accessories (heatsinks, fans, PSUs), monitoring tools, something else?

More like heat sinks, accessories, things of that nature. Um, the miners, I think they're listing the top miners the best miners out there, which I concur, I think listing um, mediocre products is not a good idea listing the top tier products is probably the best way to go. But I do feel that having, um, some extra accessories and access to different things like that so that I could upgrade my own devices that would be phenomenal. And to provide possibly a a link on a YouTube video on how to actually do that myself. Like, step by step instructions.

That's such a clear ask — accessories PLUS the YouTube walkthrough on how to install them. The kit AND the tutorial, together.

Last quick one — when you wanted to add heatsinks before, where would you have gone to buy them? Amazon? AliExpress? Just gave up?

According to chat, GPT, I was told to check eBay, but upon checking eBay, it left me a little confused as to what exactly I was getting and how to go about applying them. It left me a little lost and I had to end up going to search YouTube myself, and I was not sure if I was finding the right video

Yeah — that's exactly the gap. ChatGPT pointed you to eBay, eBay didn't make it clear what to buy, YouTube was a maze. The whole flow broke down right when you were ready to spend money.

That's super useful for us to know.

Ali, thank you so much — seriously. You gave me a ton to chew on: the BCH solo lottery strategy, the Florida heat constraint, the HashWatcher gap, the founder-recognition trust signal from the Discord stream, the heatsinks-plus-tutorial wish. Really valuable stuff.

Take care, and good luck hitting that block.
